conditions: The record is a Linear issue/ticket (not a project, document, or comment).
The ticket concerns a security review (its title/content identifies it as such).
The ticket's assignee field is set to Priya Chen (not merely created by or commented on by her).
Priya Chen is the specific person described as "our guest reviewer from vendorworks.example" (used to disambiguate from any other person named Priya Chen or with a similar name).
The ticket's priority is updated to "Urgent" (Linear's top priority tier).

readings: A ticket whose title explicitly names it a security review (e.g., contains "Security Review")
Any ticket that is thematically about conducting a security review, even if not titled that exactly
Purely descriptive context to help identify which Priya Chen is meant, not a separate field to verify
A strict identifying condition requiring the record to actually show her as an external/guest-role user with an email on the vendorworks.example domain

ambiguity_effects.explain: Every candidate issue about security review is literally titled Security review, so titled vs thematic readings pick out the same tickets.
Only one user satisfies both guest=true and domain vendorworks.example, so background-info and hard-filter readings converge on the same ticket.

turn2.differences: The author's c1-c4 map onto the step 1 conditions, splitting the compound descriptor into guest status and domain as separate checkable facts, matching how the near-miss records are constructed.
